'''''Beaucarnea''''' is a [[genus]] of [[flowering plant]]s [[native plant|native]] to Mexico and Central America.<ref name=POWO/> In the [[APG III system|APG III classification system]], it is placed in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Asparagaceae]], subfamily [[Convallarioideae]] (formerly the family Ruscaceae<ref>{{Citation |last=Chase |first=M.W. |last2=Reveal |first2=J.L. |last3=Fay |first3=M.F. |year=2009 |title=A subfamilial classification for the expanded asparagalean families Amaryllidaceae, Asparagaceae and Xanthorrhoeaceae |journal=Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society |volume=161 |issue=2 |pages=132–136 |doi=10.1111/j.1095-8339.2009.00999.x|name-list-style=amp |doi-access=free }}</ref>). ''Beaucarnea'' is sometimes treated as a synonym of the genus ''[[Nolina]]'', with the species being then transferred to that genus. However, recent research shows that ''Beaucarnea'' should be treated as an independent genus.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Rojas-Piña|first=Vanessa|last2=Olson|first2=Mark E.|last3=Alvarado-Cárdenas|first3=Leonardo O.|last4=Eguiarte|first4=Luis E.|date=2014-12-22|title=Molecular phylogenetics and morphology of Beaucarnea (Ruscaceae) as distinct from Nolina, and the submersion of Calibanus into Beaucarnea|journal=Taxon|volume=63|issue=6|pages=1193–1211|doi=10.12705/636.31}}</ref>

The species are small [[tropics|tropical]] [[xerophytic]] [[tree]]s growing to 6–10 m tall, with a trunk 20–40 cm diameter with a flared base; young plants are single-stemmed, branching only after flowering. The [[leaf|leaves]] are [[evergreen]], linear, strap-shaped, 0.5-1.8 m long and 1.5–2 cm broad, leathery in texture, with a finely [[Serration|serrated]] margin. The [[flower]]s are produced only on old trees, forming on large [[panicle]]s 75–110 cm long, the individual flowers numerous but very small (1.5 mm diameter), greenish-white, with six [[tepal]]s.

== ''Calibanus'' ==
The now defunct genus ''[[Calibanus]]'' was first formally described in 1906 by Joseph Nelson Rose,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Calibanus Rose, Contr. U.S. Natl. Herb. 10: 90 (1906) |url=https://www.ipni.org/n/24087-1 |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=International Plant Names Index www.ipni.org}}</ref> with ''Calibanus'' including two species. More recent research using molecular (phylogenetic) and morphological findings demonstrated that both former ''Calibanus'' species were closely related to ''Beaucarnea'' species, leading to both former Calibanus species being transferred to the genus ''Beaucarnea''.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Rojas-Piña |first=Vanessa |last2=Olson |first2=Mark E. |last3=Alvarado-Cárdenas |first3=Leonardo O. |last4=Eguiarte |first4=Luis E. |date=December 2014 |title=Molecular phylogenetics and morphology of Beaucarnea (Ruscaceae) as distinct from Nolina, and the submersion of Calibanus into Beaucarnea |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.12705/636.31 |journal=Taxon |language=en |volume=63 |issue=6 |pages=1193–1211 |doi=10.12705/636.31 |issn=0040-0262|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Calibanus Rose {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:297730-2 |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref>

The affected species are:

* ''Beaucarnea glassiana <small>(</small>''<small>L.Hern. & Zamudio) V.Rojas-Piña'';''</small> formally ''[[Calibanus glassianus]]'' <small>L.Hern. & Zamudio</small> 
* ''Beaucarnea hookeri'' <small>(Lem.) Trel.;</small> formerly ''[[Calibanus hookeri]]'' <small>(Lem.) Trel.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /></small>
